description: Na₄P₃H₃O₁₁ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pbcn space group. There are two inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.29-2.73 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted NaO₆ octahedra that share  a cornercorner with one NaO₆ octahedra, corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra,  an edgeedge with one NaO₆ octahedra, and  an edgeedge with one PO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 52°. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.33-2.54 Å. There are two inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four equivalent NaO₆ octahedra and corners with two equivalent PO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 51-62°. There are two shorter (1.51 Å) and two longer (1.62 Å) P-O bond lengths. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra,  a cornercorner with one PO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 40-65°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.51-1.64 Å. There are two inequivalent H sites. In the first H site, H is bonded in a linear geometry to two equivalent O atoms. Both H-O bond lengths are 1.21 Å. In the second H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to two O atoms. There is one shorter (0.99 Å) and one longer (1.74 Å) H-O bond length. There are six inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted water-like geometry to two equivalent Na and two equivalent H atoms. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to three Na and one P atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to three Na and one P atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na, one P, and one H atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na, one P, and one H atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na and two P atoms.
